You have always taken an interest in your house's accounts, and like to double check the figures. 

Your attention to detail has paid off: your vassals have been exploiting an innocuous loophole to pay less tax.
An empire is nothing without wealth. Wealth is power. Security. Safety. You can never have enough.
A clever way of avoiding paying a portion of taxes by the vassals of this house has been identified, and closed
You've been staring at the figures for hours now. Every time they tick up, your heart leaps.
Money is only as good as what it can buy.
Why hoard it when spending it can bring joy to those you care about?

You have always been good with figures - why not put that skill to use?

If you "selectively revised" your accounts, hid certain income streams, you could pay less tax to {d(Master)}.
An edit here, an account there...
There are some glaring errors in {d_s(PlayerCharacter)} accounts and it's clear {hehas(PlayerCharacter)} been avoiding paying at least some taxes.
This will come back to haunt us
Render unto your master the things that are your masters
We've found a sly way to avoid paying some of our taxes, and we're abusing it for as long as it lasts
Analysing your colony's workflow and production lines, you realise some factories could generate more income.
They just need to be properly restructured
The colony's workflow and production lines have been realigned by someone with a keen eye for detail.
We can only afford a few tweaks
The colony's workflow and production lines have been realigned by someone with a keen eye for detail but who was clearly in a hurry.
You like to take a shuttle out now and then to patrol the planet. On your latest foray you notice a weak point in the colony's defences.
Our position is more solid now
A gap in the colony's natural defenses has been reinforced by the ruler of this system, making it harder to assault.

For some time now you have been reading studies of past battles, fleet composition and strategy. 

This information could help {House} in battle.
I shall make these case studies part of our training regime
Exercises inspired by Sun Tzu and Clausewitz feature prominently in the training regimen of this house
Using the ancient classics on military strategy
It's enough that these lessons have made me a better admiral

A fleet is nothing without good leadership, and the question of how to train those officers has been bothering you recently.

You wonder if a series of war simulations and games could teach complicated strategies, logistics and battlefield tactics?
A good idea, but I lack the resources

Your security team handle espionage and unearth secrets, but sometimes a ruler needs his own insurance. You never know who to trust.

Connections and information are everything. If you gathered names, aliases, secrets, identities, connections... 

A little book can be a powerful weapon.
That's what my security team is for
A little book begins with a little secret
You have bought a little book - analogue and physical is so much more secure - and it begins to fill with names as informants whisper them in your ear.
Money talks.  Let's keep them talking
The book is hungry for names.  Let's search for more.

You adjust your hood and steal inside. The air is full of chemical smoke; lurid posters line the walls. 

You slide into the booth. "I need a name for my little book."
You'll need protection when they find out
I'll even lend you my bodyguards
For whatever reason the bodyguards of {House} seem fewer in number
A little book can cast a long shadow

Your book is gorged on names, dates, locations. Finally full. 

Most weapons are made of steel, or energy, or carbon fibre. But some are made of paper.
I am the spider of my own web
The cipher to {PlayerCharacter}'s book of secrets

{D_s(PlayerCharacter)} little book contains a wealth of secrets, all in code. But {d(DiscoveringCharacter)} got access to the book - while {he(PlayerCharacter)} slept? While {hewas(PlayerCharacter)} distracted? - and cracked the cipher.

After gifting {him(PlayerCharacter)} so many secrets, it has become a liability.
Most weapons are made of steel, or energy, or carbon fibre. But some are made of paper.
Secrecy is largely the art of guarded speech.  Unfortunately, your tongue was never tamed.
Crap, what did I just say?

While touring the colony, you inspect the homes of your poorest subjects and discover they live in appalling conditions. Drinking water is not insulated from contaminants, and mould and spores are forming in the ventilation ducts.

These people do not seem happy. If you don't improve these conditions it might foment unrest.
Some of my people live in squalor
Invest in better pipes to keep water and sewage seperate
The ruler of this system has invested in better infrastructure to transfer water and sewage around the colony structure, reducing the spread of disease.
Send cleaning crews to get rid of the mould
The ruler of this system has spent some money cleaning the warrens of tunnels and nooks in which the common folk live of the grime and mould that has built up over many years.
It's not like we're short on workers...

You are sitting down to lunch with {d(Character)}. Suddenly {he(Character)} groans; {his(Character)} breath comes in gasps; {his(Character)} eyes widen in pain, and {he(Character)} keels to the floor.
A medical team is on its way with a heart-spark, but {d(Character)} is still unconscious - perhaps dead.

No breath; no pulse. You begin to pump their chest, and fill {his(Character)} lungs with yours. It is an ancient ritual, known only to a few. 

{D(MedicalHead)} bursts in, trailing a medical team. They plug jagged electrodes to {his(Character)} chest. The room crackles with blue light as they spark {him(Character)}.

Are they alive? Are they dead? How did this happen? This can't be happening!

{D(MedicalHead)} bursts in, trailing a medical team. They plug jagged electrodes to {his(Character)} chest. The room crackles with blue light as they spark {him(Character)}.

With a crackling jolt, {d(Character)} jerks awake. {His(Character)} eyes snap wide with the terror of death; {his(Character)} lungs gasp like a thunderclap.

{D(MedicalHead)} smiles. "Sometimes Death has mercy," {he(MedicalHead)} explains. "She needs an offering of breath. And it helps that She's terrified of lightning."
Life is a gift.  It's precious.
I suppose life is short and brutal
I feel I've gained some perspective

{D(Character)} lies helpless. Limbs jerking with every shock; a brutal dance. After five minutes, everyone goes silent. After ten, it feels like a grotesque funeral.

Suddenly, a spark that catches: {d(Character)} gasps into life, lungs roaring, limbs a torrent of panic.

{D(MedicalHead)} looks on sadly. "Sometimes Death throws one back," {he(MedicalHead)} mutters. "But when you've been on the other side that long, you're never quite the same."
Ever since their brush with death, {dhas(Character)} been sickly and weak. It is as though their body never recovered.
Ever since their brush with death, {dhas(Character)}'s with has seemed slower.  It is as though their mind has been subtly impacted.

{D(Character)} lies helpless. Limbs jerking with every shock; a brutal dance. After five minutes, everyone goes silent. After ten, it feels like a grotesque funeral.

After twenty they unscrew the device. You fold {his(Character)} arms and close {his(Character)} eyes.
{Dhas(PlayerCharacter)} tried to be particularly diplomatic with {d(Ambassador)}, the ambassador from {d(AmbassadorHead)}.
{PlayerCharacter} making an effort with my ambassador
Thanks to {d_s(PlayerCharacter)} silver tongue, {d(Character)} seems to respect {him(PlayerCharacter)} more.
We should stick together: blood is everything
I'm sure you'd do anything to help me?
